info.title: AXIAM API
info.description: Access eXtended Identity and Authorization Management — REST API

get.description:
Returns the OpenID Provider metadata per OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0.
The issuer URL is taken from `AuthConfig::oauth2_issuer_url` when set,
falling back to `AuthConfig::jwt_issuer` otherwise.

Advertises only what v1 actually serves. Claims-gathering
(`claims_interaction_endpoint`) is absent because it is not implemented;
advertising an endpoint that 404s is worse than not advertising it, since a
conforming client would route to it on the strength of this document.

Returns audit entries for unauthenticated/system requests (nil tenant_id).
Requires authentication — only logged-in users can query system audit logs.

post.description:
Authenticate a device via its client certificate (mTLS).
The certificate must be bound to a service account.

403.description: Certificate not bound to a service account

post.description:
Consumes the state row (single-use), runs the verified OIDC flow from
plan 04-02 (nonce from DB — not caller-supplied), provisions or links the
user, and returns Set-Cookie response (no token in body).

Generates a server-side state+nonce pair, persists it in
`federation_login_state` (10-min TTL), and returns the IdP authorization
URL.  No JWT required — this is the first step of first-time SSO (D-22).
Confirm MFA enrollment and complete login using a setup token.

401.description: Invalid or expired setup token / TOTP code

post.description:
Start MFA enrollment using a setup token (issued during login when
MFA is enforced but not yet configured).

Returns the same three outcomes as `POST /api/v1/auth/login` — `200` with
session cookies, `202` for an MFA challenge, `403` for MFA setup — so a
client can share one result handler across both login paths.

Note what this response does *not* carry, where the SRP one did: a server
proof. Under SRP the client had to verify `M2` itself or it would have
authenticated to a server that never knew the verifier. RFC 9807's AKE
authenticates the server as part of the handshake — a client that
successfully opens `KE2` has already proved the server holds the record —
so there is nothing left for the client to check afterwards, and an SDK
cannot forget to.

200.description: Login successful; tokens arrive as cookies

401.description: Invalid credentials, expired session, or unknown identity

400.description: Malformed KE1 or missing workspace identity

404.description: OPAQUE is not enabled for this tenant

503.description: OPAQUE is enabled but the server has no keys configured

200.description: OPRF evaluation and the KSF parameters to stretch with

400.description: Malformed registration request or missing workspace identity

404.description: OPAQUE is not enabled for this tenant

503.description: OPAQUE is enabled but the server has no keys configured

post.description:
Creates a new email verification token and enqueues it for async
delivery via the mail queue (D-14).  Always returns `{"sent": true}`
to prevent email enumeration (D-15) — regardless of whether the email
exists, is already verified, or has hit a rate limit.

Initiates a password reset by enqueuing an `OutboundMailMessage` to the
async mail queue.  Always returns `{"sent": true}` to prevent email
enumeration (D-15) — regardless of whether the email exists, the user is
federated, delivery later succeeds, or the rate limit is exceeded.

Confirms a password reset using a one-time token and a new
password. The token is consumed atomically.

Returns `{"reset": true}` on success, or 400 with policy
violations if the new password is too weak.

400.description: Invalid token or password policy violation

get.description:
Password reset would otherwise be a permanent hole in OPAQUE coverage. The
reset page is unauthenticated and holds only a token and a tenant id, so it
cannot tell whether the tenant expects an enrolment. Without that, every
"forgot password" would leave the account with a record for a password it
no longer has, and under `opaque_mode: required` would leave it unable to
log in at all.

# What this no longer discloses

The SRP version returned the account's username, because that string was
inside the client-side key derivation and the reset page had no other way
to learn it. That was defensible — the caller holds a token delivered to
the account's own email — but it is better not to need the argument.
OPAQUE does not bind to the username, so it is not returned.

An attacker without a valid token still gets `404` and learns nothing — the
same answer for a wrong token, an expired token, and a token for a tenant that
does not exist.

The token is **read, not consumed**: this is a lookup, and burning the
single-use token here would break the reset it is meant to enable.

parameters.name: tenant_id
parameters.description: Tenant the reset link was issued for

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Raw reset token from the emailed link

post.description:
Verifies a user's email using a one-time token. The token is
consumed atomically — replaying the same token returns an error.

Complete a WebAuthn passkey authentication ceremony.  On success
a session is created and access/refresh tokens are issued.

Begin a WebAuthn passkey authentication ceremony.  Requires a
valid MFA challenge token (obtained from the login flow).

Complete a WebAuthn passkey registration ceremony.

X3 wave 3: routes through
[`WebauthnService::finish_registration_for_policy`], which dispatches on
which ceremony the state token was minted for and re-checks it against
the policy **currently** in force (see that method's docs for why a
policy tightened mid-ceremony still denies).

403.description: Denied by the tenant's attestation policy (this security key model is not permitted by your organization)

post.description:
Begin a WebAuthn passkey registration ceremony for the
authenticated user.

X3 wave 3: routes through
[`WebauthnService::start_registration_for_policy`], resolving the
tenant's [`WebauthnAttestationPolicy`](axiam_core::models::webauthn_policy::WebauthnAttestationPolicy)
first (an absent row is `WebauthnAttestationPolicy::default()` — `mode:
none`, today's behavior unchanged). This is the single call-site switch
that makes attestation enforcement live: calling
[`WebauthnService::start_registration`] directly here would silently
downgrade every tenant to the unattested ceremony regardless of policy.

503.description: Attestation policy requires attestation but no FIDO metadata is available (W2-D3 fail-closed)

post.description:
Evaluate a single authorization check for the authenticated caller (or, if
the caller holds `authz:check_as`, for an arbitrary subject).

`tenant_id` is always taken from the JWT — it cannot be supplied in the body.

403.description: Forbidden — caller lacks authz:check_as for subject_id override

post.description:
Evaluate an ordered list of authorization checks.  Returns results in the
same order and length as the input `checks` array.

If **any** check in the batch includes a `subject_id`, the caller must hold
`authz:check_as` — the permission is verified once up front (not per item).

403.description: Forbidden — caller lacks authz:check_as for subject_id override

items.description:
A tenant-level certificate for users, services, or IoT devices.

Certificates are signed by the organization's CA. The private key is
returned once on generation and never stored by AXIAM.

issuer_ca_id.description: The CA certificate that signed this certificate.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata (e.g., device serial, user ID binding).

tenant_id.description: The tenant this certificate belongs to.

post.summary: Record the user's approval or refusal.

get.summary: Look up a pending grant by the code the user typed.

parameters.name: user_code
parameters.description:
The code as the user typed it. Case, spaces and dashes are normalized
server-side, so `WXYZ-1234`, `wxyz 1234` and `WXYZ1234` are one code.

post.description:
Builds the authorization URL for the external OIDC provider. The caller
is responsible for generating and storing `state` and `nonce` values
for CSRF and replay protection.

TODO(T19.9): This endpoint currently requires authentication, making it
usable only for account-linking (already-authenticated users). Add
separate unauthenticated federation login endpoints that complete the
external flow and return access/refresh tokens for first-time login.

Handles the callback from the external OIDC provider after user
authentication. Exchanges the authorization code for tokens,
validates the ID token, and provisions or links the local user.

items.description:
A group of users that can access resources based on their roles
and permissions. Groups simplify role management by allowing roles
to be assigned to a group rather than individual users.
Public-safe user representation (no password_hash, no mfa_secret).

email_verified.description:
True when the user's email address has been verified
(`email_verified_at` is set). Exposed for the admin UI / profile.

failed_login_attempts.description: Number of consecutive failed login attempts.

is_locked.description: Whether the account is currently locked (locked_until is in the future).

locked_until.description: Timestamp until which the account is locked, if any.

post.description:
Fetches (or, when `AXIAM__PKI__MDS_BLOB_PATH` is set, loads locally),
verifies, and ingests the FIDO MDS3 BLOB. Refuses to run when MDS
ingestion is disabled (`AXIAM__PKI__MDS_ENABLED=false`, the default) —
per `PkiConfig`'s documented contract, the master switch being off means
this endpoint makes no outbound call at all, not just that the
background job doesn't run.

200.description: Ingestion attempt completed (see `outcome` — a rejected rollback or no-op refresh is still a 200, not an error)

503.description: Fetch or cryptographic verification of the BLOB failed

200.description: Current FIDO MDS3 ingestion status (never-ingested returns nulls, not a 404)

jwks.description:
X5.1 — echoed so an operator can confirm which key source is registered.
The document itself is public key material, so returning it leaks
nothing; a `jwks_uri` is likewise public by construction.

profile.description:
X5.1 — the registered posture and mTLS credentials. Read-back matters:
an operator auditing which clients are financial-grade should be able
to answer it from this endpoint rather than from the database.

items.description:
An organization groups multiple tenants under a single administrative entity.

Organizations represent companies, departments, or business units.
CA certificates are registered at the organization level, enabling
a hierarchical trust model across all tenants.

A CA (Certificate Authority) certificate at the organization level.

CA certificates are the root of trust for all tenant certificates
within the organization. Private keys for signing CAs are encrypted
with AES-256-GCM and stored separately; non-signing CAs only store
the public certificate.

organization_id.description: The organization this CA belongs to.

subject.description: The certificate subject (e.g., `CN=ACME Corp Root CA`).

404.description: No email configuration set for this organization

items.description:
A tenant is an isolated context within an organization.

Each tenant has its own set of users, roles, permissions, resources,
certificates, and configuration. Tenants can represent environments
(dev/staging/prod) or separate business contexts.

organization_id.description: The organization this tenant belongs to.

slug.description: URL-safe unique identifier within the organization (e.g., `production`).

status.description: Lifecycle status. New tenants default to [`TenantStatus::Active`].

items.description: An OpenPGP key stored by AXIAM.

last_seen_at.description:
When this reactor last consumed from its queue. `null` means it has
never connected — which the admin UI shows differently from "connected
once, silent since".

recent_timeout_count.description:
R2.3: dispatch failures against this registration in the last 24h
whose cause was a timeout (as opposed to a rejected reply, a transport
failure, or overload), capped at 100 — a health signal read from the
audit trail R2.2 started writing, not a replacement for the audit log
itself (`GET /api/v1/audit-log` is that).

recent_veto_count.description:
R2.3: operations this reactor's own reply *denied* in the last 24h,
capped at 100. Distinct from `recent_timeout_count`: a veto is the
reactor working as designed; a timeout is the reactor not answering.

400.description: Unknown event, non-interceptable event, or out-of-range timeout

get.description:
Served rather than documented so an admin UI, an SDK generator and an
operator all read the same list the dispatcher enforces. A hand-maintained
copy in the docs is a copy that goes stale on the next hook added.

parent_id.description: Parent resource ID for hierarchical organization. `None` for root resources.

uma_registered_by.description:
The `client_id` that registered this resource through the UMA
Protection API (X2), or `None` for a resource created any other way.

Read-only from every ordinary path: [`UpdateResource`] cannot set it and
[`CreateResource`] cannot either, so the only writer is the
resource-registration handler. That is deliberate — the field backs a
provenance badge in the admin UI, and a provenance marker anyone can
write is decoration that reads like evidence.

is_global.description: Global roles grant permissions across all resources.

get.description: Lists the groups directly assigned this role.

parameters.name: resource_id
parameters.description:
If provided, only removes the assignment for this specific resource.
If omitted, removes the global (unscoped) assignment.

get.description:
Lists the users directly assigned this role (the inverse of
`GET /users/{id}/roles`). Used by the role detail page's members panel.

parameters.name: resource_id
parameters.description:
If provided, only removes the assignment for this specific resource.
If omitted, removes the global (unscoped) assignment.

201.description: Token minted; the handle is returned once

400.description: Invalid lifetime, or the named user cannot use SCIM

delete.description:
Revokes rather than deletes: the row is what lets an operator later answer
"was this credential still live on the day of the incident?", and a
deleted row answers nothing.

get.description:
Returns the effective (merged) security settings for the
authenticated user's tenant. Org baseline + tenant overrides.

put.description:
Set tenant-level overrides. Only fields that are **more restrictive**
than the org baseline are accepted. Omit a field (set to `null`) to
inherit from the org.

404.description: No email configuration override set for this tenant

200.description: Tenant email configuration override updated (secrets omitted)
Effective WebAuthn attestation policy (defaults returned when no policy row exists — D5)

400.description: Config error — e.g. require_fido_certified/min_certification set with mode: none

200.description: Per-credential compliance report against the current policy — never mutates or revokes anything

items.description: Public-safe user representation (no password_hash, no mfa_secret).

email_verified.description:
True when the user's email address has been verified
(`email_verified_at` is set). Exposed for the admin UI / profile.

failed_login_attempts.description: Number of consecutive failed login attempts.

is_locked.description: Whether the account is currently locked (locked_until is in the future).

post.description:
Creates a user and atomically records a `terms_of_service` consent row
(REQ-8 / Art. 7 proof of consent).  IP address and User-Agent are
captured for the consent record.

get.description: List all MFA methods registered for a user.

403.description: Cannot view another user's MFA methods

delete.description:
Remove a specific MFA method. Returns 400 if it is the last
method and MFA is enabled.

403.description: Cannot delete another user's MFA methods

post.description:
Reset MFA for a user — disables MFA, clears the secret, and
revokes all existing sessions. Requires admin access (caller must
be in the same tenant).

Resets a locked user account: clears `locked_until`, resets
`failed_login_attempts` to 0, and sets status back to `Active`.

items.description: Webhook response — omits the shared secret.

get.description:
The user must be authenticated (redirected to login first if not).
On success, redirects to `redirect_uri?code=...&state=...`.
On error, redirects with `?error=...&error_description=...&state=...`.

parameters.name: request_uri
parameters.description:
B5 — a `urn:ietf:params:oauth:request_uri:` value obtained from
`/oauth2/par`. Mutually exclusive with the inline parameters above.

post.summary: Build an OAuth2 JSON error response with the appropriate HTTP status.
post.description:
`POST /oauth2/device_authorization` — RFC 8628 §3.1–3.2 (B2).

Issues a `device_code` (the secret the device polls with), a short
`user_code` (the string a human reads off a screen and types elsewhere),
and the `verification_uri` to send them to.

**Unauthenticated by design.** RFC 8628 exists for input-constrained public
clients — a television, a CLI, an IoT sensor — none of which can keep a
client secret, so there is no secret to present. What is still verified is
that `client_id` names a real client in this tenant that is registered for
this grant; without that check any string could mint pending grants and
exhaust the user-code space, which is a denial of service against every
legitimate device at once.

The endpoint carries its own rate-limit bucket (see `server.rs`) rather
than sharing the generic token bucket: it is unauthenticated and it
allocates state, which is a different abuse profile from the token
endpoint's.

get.description:
Ends the session named by `id_token_hint` and notifies every client that
participated in it (Back-Channel Logout 1.0), then either redirects to an
allow-listed `post_logout_redirect_uri` or renders AXIAM's own logged-out
page.

# The redirect is the whole security surface

This endpoint is reachable without authentication by design — a user whose
session has already expired must still be able to complete a logout — so an
unvalidated `post_logout_redirect_uri` would be an open redirect on an
unauthenticated endpoint. It is honoured **only** on exact match against
the identified client's `post_logout_redirect_uris`.

A non-matching URI does not fail the request: the session is still ended
and AXIAM renders its own page. Refusing to log a user out because their RP
sent a bad parameter would be the wrong failure — they asked to log out.

# Why an unverifiable hint cannot end a session

Without a verifiable `id_token_hint` there is nothing to identify but the
browser's own AXIAM cookie, so the endpoint ends the cookie session if
there is one and does nothing otherwise. It deliberately does **not** fall
back to "end every session for the subject named in an unverified
parameter": that is a denial-of-service primitive handed to anyone who
knows a user id.

# No confirmation prompt

RP-Initiated Logout 1.0 §2 permits one, and a prompt is the mitigation for
logout CSRF. We take the other side deliberately: a forced logout is a
nuisance, not a privilege escalation, and a prompt shown on every logout is
trained away within a week.

parameters.name: id_token_hint
parameters.description:
A previously-issued ID token identifying the session to end. The only
*authenticated* statement of which session and client this is about.

parameters.name: post_logout_redirect_uri
parameters.description:
Where to send the browser afterwards. Honoured only on the identified
client's allow-list, by exact match.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Echoed verbatim on a redirect that actually happens. Never interpreted.

parameters.name: client_id
parameters.description: Fallback identification when no `id_token_hint` is supplied.

302.description: Session ended; redirected to an allow-listed URI

post.description:
Accepts form-encoded body. Returns an `IntrospectionResponse` with
`active: true/false` and optional metadata.

get.description:
Returns the public signing keys used by the authorization server
so that relying parties can verify JWTs without sharing a secret.

B3: served from an in-process cache (`state.oauth2_jwks_cache`) keyed by
a hash of the source PEM, with a `Cache-Control: public, max-age=<n>`
header (configurable, default 300s) and a strong `ETag`. Clients that
send a matching `If-None-Match` get `304 Not Modified` with no body;
clients that ignore caching headers entirely still get the identical
`200 OK` + JWKS body they always did -- this is a pure additive change.
See `axiam_oauth2::jwks_cache` module docs for the cache design and the
documented limitations (no key-rotation mechanism exists yet; the
endpoint serves one global, not per-tenant, key set).

post.description:
Accepts an authorization request over a direct, client-authenticated POST
and returns an opaque `request_uri` to put in the browser redirect instead
of the parameters. What travels through the user agent is then a random
string that cannot be edited into meaning something else.

**Authenticated, unlike `/oauth2/device_authorization`.** That is the whole
point: the parameters stop travelling through the browser, and the ones
that arrive are attributable to a client that proved it holds the secret.

Answers `201`, not `200` — RFC 9126 §2.2 specifies Created, and the
response names a resource that did not exist before the call.

Accepts form-encoded body. Always returns 200 per the spec — invalid
tokens are silently ignored.

Accepts form-encoded body per RFC 6749. Supports authorization_code,
client_credentials, and refresh_token grant types. The `tenant_id` is
passed as a query parameter since the token endpoint is unauthenticated
(the client is authenticating itself here).

get.description:
Returns claims about the authenticated user. Requires a valid
Bearer access token. Email and username are included based on
the scopes present in the access token.

post.description:
# Who may call this

A **Protection API Token**: an ordinary AXIAM access token carrying the
`uma_protection` scope. Two further conditions, both deliberate:

1. **The token must be an OAuth2 client token** (`sub_kind` =
   `OAuth2Client`). A ticket is bound to the `client_id` that minted it, and
   for a client-credentials token `sub` *is* the `client_id`. A user token
   has no client identity in it, so binding one would mean inventing a
   value and calling it a binding.
2. **The scope is checked here, not by a route guard.** The `uma_protection`
   scope is what makes an access token a PAT; nothing else about the token
   distinguishes it.

get.description:
Lists only the resources **this client** registered. FedAuthz says the
listing is of the resource sets the PAT's owner registered, and a resource
server has no business enumerating the tenant's whole resource tree through
an endpoint whose only credential is a protection scope.

post.description:
Creates the resource **and** its declared scopes. The scope set is what the
permission endpoint later validates ticket requests against, so registering
a resource with no scopes produces one that can never appear in a ticket —
legal, and worth knowing.

put.description:
The scope list is **replaced**, not merged: FedAuthz defines the update as
putting the resource set's new state, and a merge would make it impossible
to remove a scope. Removing a scope narrows what tickets may be requested,
so a silent merge would keep an authority the resource server tried to drop.

ApiProviderConfig.description:
API-based provider configuration (SendGrid, Postmark, Resend, Brevo).

`api_key` follows the same write-only + omit-preserving contract as
[`SmtpConfig::password`] (D-01/D-02).

api_url.description: Override base URL (useful for testing / self-hosted instances).

AttestationDenyReason.description:
Why [`evaluate`] denied a registration. Machine-readable — goes to the
audit record; the end user sees a fixed, non-specific message (D7/D11).

AttestationMode.description:
What attestation conveyance a registration ceremony requests, and whether
the policy is enforced at all.

`None` is the default and reproduces today's behavior byte-for-byte:
`evaluate` allows every registration unconditionally, with no MDS lookup
(D8 step 1).

BatchCheckAccessBody.description: Body for a batch authorization check.

checks.description: Ordered list of checks to evaluate.

BatchCheckAccessResponse.description: Result of a batch authorization check.

results.description: Ordered results — same length and order as the input `checks`.

BindCertificate.description: Request to bind a certificate to a service account.

CaCertificate.description:
A CA (Certificate Authority) certificate at the organization level.

CA certificates are the root of trust for all tenant certificates
within the organization. Private keys for signing CAs are encrypted
with AES-256-GCM and stored separately; non-signing CAs only store
the public certificate.

organization_id.description: The organization this CA belongs to.

subject.description: The certificate subject (e.g., `CN=ACME Corp Root CA`).

Certificate.description:
A tenant-level certificate for users, services, or IoT devices.

Certificates are signed by the organization's CA. The private key is
returned once on generation and never stored by AXIAM.

issuer_ca_id.description: The CA certificate that signed this certificate.

metadata.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata (e.g., device serial, user ID binding).

tenant_id.description: The tenant this certificate belongs to.

CertificateStatus.description: Status of a certificate in its lifecycle.

CertificateType.description: The purpose for which a certificate was issued.

CertificationLevel.description:
FIDO certification level, as recorded in an MDS `statusReports` entry's
`FIDO_CERTIFIED*` status.

Variant order is significant: `derive(PartialOrd, Ord)` gives `L1 < L1Plus
< L2 < L2Plus < L3 < L3Plus`, which `WebauthnAttestationPolicy::evaluate`
(D8 step 9) relies on directly for the `min_certification` boundary
check (`entry_level >= policy_min`).

CheckAccessBody.description: Body for a single authorization check.

resource_id.description: The resource UUID the action targets.

subject_id.description:
Subject to check on behalf of.

When `Some`, the caller must hold `authz:check_as` (T-15-01).
When `None`, the check is performed for the authenticated caller.

CheckAccessResponse.description: Result of a single authorization check.

reason.description: Engine-provided deny reason (T-15-02: generic string only, no resource-structure hints).

reason_code.description:
B1: machine-readable decision reason — `allowed`, `no_grant`, or
`denied_by_rule` (SDK contract §11).

Both refusals still return `allowed: false` and still map to 403, so a
client that reads only `allowed` is unaffected. The distinction matters
to the person on the other end: `no_grant` means "ask an admin for
access", `denied_by_rule` means "an admin has already decided" — and a
UI that cannot tell them apart sends users to raise tickets that will
be refused.

T-15-02 still holds: this is a fixed, closed vocabulary of three
values. It says which *kind* of decision was made, never which rule
made it or where in the resource tree it sits.

ClientAuthMethod.description:
How a client proves its identity at the token endpoint (RFC 8705 §2,
OIDC Core §9 naming).

Only the methods AXIAM actually implements are representable. There is
deliberately no `none` variant: every AXIAM client is confidential today
(see `handle_authorization_code`), and adding a public-client value here
before the rest of the server understands one would let an operator
register a client whose authentication is silently skipped.

ClientProfile.description:
Which security posture a client is registered under (X5.1).

This is the FAPI "one switch". FAPI 2.0 is not a single feature but a
bundle of constraints — mandatory PAR, mandatory PKCE with `S256`,
mandatory strong client authentication, mandatory sender-constrained
tokens, and a refusal of every relaxation the base specs permit. Encoding
them as one profile rather than a dozen independent booleans means an
operator cannot register a client that is *nearly* FAPI, and a reviewer
can answer "is this client financial-grade?" by reading one field.

The same philosophy as the rate-limit postures: ordinary clients see no
behaviour change at all, because [`Standard`](Self::Standard) is the serde
default and every row written before schema v38 decodes to it.

CnfClaim.description:
RFC 7800 confirmation claim, carrying either or both of the two
sender-constraining methods AXIAM implements.

Deliberately a struct of optional fields rather than an enum: RFC 7800
permits several confirmation methods in one claim, and a token that arrived
carrying a method AXIAM does not implement must still round-trip through
`serde` intact rather than fail to decode. What it must *not* do is
validate — see [`CnfClaim::names_only_known_methods`], which answers `false`
for exactly that case, and [`verify_token_binding`], which treats it as a
refusal.

# Both at once is a conjunction, never a disjunction

A `cnf` carrying both `x5t#S256` and `jkt` means the holder must satisfy
**both**. Reading it as "either will do" would let a client that had asked
for two constraints be used with one — which is strictly weaker than what it
asked for, and is the failure mode of every "check whichever we can" binding
validator.

jkt.description:
RFC 9449 §6.1 `jkt` — the base64url-encoded (unpadded) SHA-256 RFC 7638
thumbprint of the public key whose DPoP proof was presented at the token
endpoint.

A token carrying this is usable only by a caller that can sign a fresh
DPoP proof with the corresponding private key, on every request. That is
a different cost class from `x5t#S256` — an asymmetric verification per
request rather than one SHA-256 — and `axiam_oauth2::dpop`'s module docs
say so with a measured number.

x5t#S256.description:
RFC 8705 §3.1 `x5t#S256` — the base64url-encoded (unpadded) SHA-256
digest of the DER-encoded client certificate the token was issued to.

compliant.description:
`false` only for a genuine policy violation
([`ComplianceStatus::NonCompliant`]) — a credential with no recorded
AAGUID ([`ComplianceStatus::Unknown`], D9's pre-X3 case) is always
`true` here, never reported as a violation.

name.description:
The credential's user-assigned name (`WebauthnCredential::name`),
not the owning user's account name.

reason.description:
`None` only when `compliant` and the credential has a recorded
AAGUID; set for every non-compliant *and* every "unknown" (pre-X3)
credential.

oneOf.description:
OPAQUE registration record for `new_password`, built client-side.

Without this, reset would be the hole in OPAQUE coverage: a tenant could
run `opaque_mode = required`, and every "forgot password" would still put a
plaintext password on the wire and leave the account with a verifier for
a password it no longer has.

CreateCaCertificate.description: Fields required to generate a new CA certificate (user-facing DTO).

CreateCertificate.description: Fields required to generate a new tenant certificate (user-facing DTO).

allowed_algorithms.description:
Accepted JWT signing algorithms (OIDC) or signature algorithms (SAML).
Defaults to `["RS256"]` when not provided (CQ-B40/REQ-14 AC-5).

attribute_map.description: Maps external IdP attributes to AXIAM user fields.

client_id.description: OAuth2 client ID registered with the external IdP.

client_secret.description: OAuth2 client secret registered with the external IdP.

idp_signing_cert_pem.description:
PEM-encoded X.509 certificate for verifying SAML assertions or
OIDC signatures (CQ-B40/REQ-14 AC-5).  Required for SAML configs.

metadata_url.description: OIDC discovery URL or SAML metadata URL.

provider.description: Display name for the identity provider (e.g., "Google", "Okta").

oneOf.description: X4 external token-exchange trust. Omitted means disabled.

description.description: Description of what this rule monitors.

events.description: Event types that trigger this rule.

backchannel_logout_uri.description:
B5 — where OIDC back-channel logout tokens are delivered. Omit for a
client that does not participate.

dpop_bound_access_tokens.description:
RFC 9449 §5.2 — issue DPoP-bound (sender-constrained) access tokens to
this client. Independent of both the authentication method and
`tls_client_certificate_bound_access_tokens`; a client may ask for both
constraints, and a token carrying both must satisfy both.

dpop_require_nonce.description:
RFC 9449 §8 — require this client's DPoP proofs to carry a
server-issued nonce.

**Not implemented in this build (SEC-097).** `true` is refused with
`400`; only `false` (the default) is accepted. Nothing reads the stored
value, so accepting `true` would persist and echo back a security
switch that does nothing. DPoP proofs are made single-use at the token
endpoint by `jti` replay detection instead — see
`docs/security-profiles.md`.

grant_types.description: Grant types this client is authorized to use.

jwks.description:
RFC 7591 §2 — the client's public key set, inline, for
`private_key_jwt`. Exactly one of `jwks` and `jwks_uri` may be set.

jwks_uri.description:
RFC 7591 §2 — where the client publishes its public key set. Must be an
absolute `https` URL, and is fetched through the SSRF-guarded JWKS
cache, which refuses private and loopback addresses.

post_logout_redirect_uris.description:
B5 — allow-list for RP-initiated logout's `post_logout_redirect_uri`.
Separate from `redirect_uris` on purpose: that list receives
authorization codes, this one receives a browser after logout.

profile.description:
X5.1 — the security posture this client is registered under.

`"standard"` (the default) is every AXIAM client that has ever existed.
`"fapi2"` turns on the whole FAPI 2.0 constraint bundle at once, and
the registration is refused unless it also sets `require_par`, a strong
`token_endpoint_auth_method` (either mTLS method or `private_key_jwt`),
and at least one sender-constraining mechanism
(`tls_client_certificate_bound_access_tokens` or
`dpop_bound_access_tokens`). See the FAPI operator guide.

redirect_uris.description:
Allowed redirect URIs (must be HTTPS, except localhost for dev).
SEC-089: this list doubles as the token-exchange audience allow-list
— adding a URI here also authorises it as a token audience for this
client, so review additions on exchange-capable clients with that in
mind (see `docs/api/token-exchange.md#audience`).

require_par.description:
B5 — require this client to push its authorization parameters to
`/oauth2/par` (RFC 9126) rather than sending them through the browser.

self_signed_tls_client_auth_thumbprints.description:
Accepted certificate thumbprints for `self_signed_tls_client_auth`,
as base64url-unpadded SHA-256 digests of the DER certificate (the same
`x5t#S256` encoding as the `cnf` claim). More than one permits an
overlapping rotation.

tls_client_auth_subject_dn.description:
RFC 8705 §2.1.2 — expected certificate subject DN, RFC 4514 form.
Exactly one of the three `tls_client_auth_*` parameters may be set.

tls_client_certificate_bound_access_toke.description:
RFC 8705 §3.4 — issue certificate-bound (sender-constrained) access
tokens to this client. Independent of the authentication method.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description:
X5.1 — how this client authenticates at the token endpoint
(RFC 8705 §2). Defaults to `client_secret_post`.

CreateOrganization.description: Fields required to create a new organization.

CreatePgpKey.description: User-facing DTO for generating a new PGP key.

email.description: Email for the OpenPGP User ID.
Email for the OpenPGP User ID.

oneOf.description: Omit to take the strictest default among `events`.

timeout_ms.description: Omit to take the 500 ms default. Capped at 5 000 ms.

expires_in_days.description:
Lifetime in days. Defaults to the deployment maximum, and is refused
above it.

user_id.description:
The tenant user the token authenticates as. Must already hold
`scim:provision` — see [`create`].

provisioning_token.description: The plaintext handle — shown once, never retrievable again.

CreateScimTokenResponse.description:
The one-time reveal. Same shape as service-account creation: the secret is
returned once and only its hash is kept.

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the account's purpose.
Optional human-readable description of the account's purpose.

CreateTenant.description: Fields required to create a new tenant.

CreateTenantRequest.description: Request body for tenant creation (organization_id comes from the URL path).

password.description: Raw password (will be hashed with Argon2id before storage).

oneOf.description:
OPAQUE registration record for `password`, built client-side.

The server cannot derive this — the envelope is sealed under a key only
the client can compute — so it has to arrive with the request or not at
all. Required under `opaque_mode = required`, where a user created
without one could never authenticate.

Obtained by calling `POST /api/v1/auth/opaque/register/start` first and
carrying its `opaque_session` through, which is the one structural
difference from the SRP verifier this replaces: a verifier could be
computed offline from a self-chosen salt, whereas a record needs the
server's OPRF evaluation.

secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 shared secret for signing payloads.

url.description: The HTTPS URL to deliver events to.

approved.description:
`true` approves, `false` refuses. A refusal is recorded rather than
ignored: it is what lets the polling device stop immediately instead
of waiting out the full grant lifetime after the user has already said
no (see `device_service`'s polling table).

ok.description: `false` for unknown, expired, or already-decided codes alike.

DeviceAuthResponse.description: Response returned when a device authenticates via certificate.

device_code.description: The secret the device polls with. Returned once; only its hash is kept.

user_code.description: The short code the user reads off the device and types.

verification_uri.description: Where the user should go to enter it.

verification_uri_complete.description:
The same URI with the code pre-filled, for devices that can render a
QR code. RFC 8628 §3.3.1 — optional, but it is the difference between
a user typing eight characters and scanning.

EmailConfig.description: Fully resolved email configuration (all fields present).

scope_id.description: The org_id or tenant_id this config belongs to.

EmailConfigOverride.description:
Partial tenant overrides for email configuration.
`None` = inherit from org baseline.

oneOf.description: Full provider replacement (no partial merge within a provider).

EncryptedExport.description: Result of encrypting data with a PGP public key.

FailurePolicy.description:
What the server does when an interceptor does not produce a usable reply —
timeout, transport failure, bad signature, stale nonce, or a patch the
allow-list rejects.

private_key_pem.description: PEM-encoded private key — returned only on generation.

GeneratedCaCertificate.description:
Response returned when a CA certificate is generated.

Includes the private key PEM, which is returned **once** and never
stored or retrievable again.

private_key_pem.description: PEM-encoded private key — returned only on generation.

GeneratedCertificate.description:
Response returned when a tenant certificate is generated.

Includes the private key PEM, returned **once** and never stored.

private_key_armored.description:
ASCII-armored private key — returned only on generation for `Export` keys.
For `AuditSigning` keys this is `None` (private key is server-side only).

GeneratedPgpKey.description: Response returned when a PGP key is generated.

effect.description:
B1: `"allow"` (the default) or `"deny"`.

A deny grant **overrides every allow**, at any depth of the resource
hierarchy and at equal specificity — it is not most-specific-wins. See
`claude_dev/deny-override-design.md` for the precedence table and for
why that trade was made.

Omitting the field means `"allow"`, so every existing client keeps
working unchanged and no migration is required.

Group.description:
A group of users that can access resources based on their roles
and permissions. Groups simplify role management by allowing roles
to be assigned to a group rather than individual users.

IntrospectRequest.description:
RFC 7662 token introspection request.

Same credential shape, and for the same reason, as [`RevokeRequest`].

oneOf.description:
RFC 8705 §3.3 `cnf` — present only when the introspected token is
certificate-bound (X5.1).

RFC 8705 requires the authorization server to expose the confirmation
through introspection, because a resource server doing token
introspection rather than local JWT validation has no other way to
learn that the token it is holding is not a bearer token. Omitting it
would leave every introspecting resource server treating bound tokens
as unbound — the exact failure the binding exists to prevent.

permissions.description:
UMA 2.0 `permissions` (X2) — present only when the introspected token
is an RPT.

Keycloak's authorization services put the same array under the same key
in an introspection response, so a resource server migrating from
Keycloak reads an AXIAM RPT without a translation layer.

This is **echoed from the token, not re-evaluated**. Introspection
answers "what does this token say", and the permissions claim is a
record of a decision made when the RPT was minted. A resource server
that needs a live answer must ask the authorization endpoints — which is
why RPT lifetime is bounded rather than long.

KeyAlgorithm.description: The type of key algorithm used for a certificate.

LoginSuccessResponse.description:
Login success response body.

Tokens are delivered via `Set-Cookie` headers — not in this body.

LoginUserInfo.description: User info included in login/me responses.

org_slug.description:
26-05 (D-14): same contract as `tenant_slug`, resolved via the
tenant's `organization_id`.

tenant_id.description:
23-06: exposes the caller's raw tenant_id UUID so the frontend can
carry it into tenant-scoped unauthenticated calls that require it
(e.g. `resendVerification`'s `ResendVerificationRequest.tenant_id`)
without re-deriving it from a slug. Already known server-side from
the validated JWT / AuthenticatedUser extractor — this only exposes
it, it does not widen trust.

tenant_slug.description:
26-05 (D-14): lets the frontend restore the selected tenant after a
hard reload without a redundant lookup. Resolved strictly from the
authenticated user's own `tenant_id` (never request input — T-26-05-01)
and omitted (not an error) when the lookup fails (D-15).

oneOf.description: First-ever ingestion — no stored serial existed.
A newer BLOB replaced the stored entries.
The fetched BLOB's `no` equalled the stored serial — a no-op refresh.

The fetched BLOB's `no` was lower than the stored serial — rejected
as a rollback attempt. Nothing was written.

MdsRefreshOutcome.description:
`POST /api/v1/mds/refresh` response — the outcome of one ingestion
attempt (mirrors `axiam_db::mds_ingest::MdsIngestOutcome`).

MdsStatusResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/mds/status` response. `no`/`next_update`/`last_refreshed_at`
are `None` and `stale` is `false` when MDS has never been ingested — a
meaningful, valid answer ("nothing ingested yet"), not an error.

NotificationEventType.description: Events that can trigger an admin notification.

NotificationRule.description: A notification rule that determines which events trigger admin emails.

OAuth2ClientCreatedResponse.description: Response for client creation -- includes the one-time plaintext secret.

jwks.description:
X5.1 — echoed so an operator can confirm which key source is registered.
The document itself is public key material, so returning it leaks
nothing; a `jwks_uri` is likewise public by construction.

profile.description:
X5.1 — the registered posture and mTLS credentials. Read-back matters:
an operator auditing which clients are financial-grade should be able
to answer it from this endpoint rather than from the database.

config_id.description: ID of the federation config to use.

nonce.description: Nonce for replay protection (generated by the caller).

redirect_uri.description: Redirect URI the external IdP should return the user to.

state.description: CSRF state value (generated by the caller).

url.description: The full authorization URL to redirect the user to.

code.description: Authorization code returned by the external IdP.

config_id.description: ID of the federation config used in the authorization request.

nonce.description:
Client-supplied nonce (SECHRD-07/D-04: retained for backward
compatibility with older callers, but IGNORED for verification —
`expected_nonce` always comes from the server-side `FederationLoginState`
row looked up via `state`, never from this field).

redirect_uri.description: Redirect URI that was used in the authorization request.

state.description:
CSRF state value from the authorization request. Used to look up the
server-side `FederationLoginState` row that holds the real nonce
(SECHRD-07/D-04) — required so the callback can find its login state.

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description:
RFC 9207 §3 — X5.1. AXIAM emits `iss` on **every** authorization
response, success and error alike, for every client, so this is
unconditionally true. See `handlers::oauth2::append_issuer` for why it
is not made conditional.

backchannel_logout_session_supported.description:
The claim that AXIAM puts `sid` in its logout tokens — which it does,
unconditionally. An RP reads this to know it can match a logout token
to one session rather than having to end every session for the subject.

device_authorization_endpoint.description:
RFC 8628 §4 — B2. Advertised unconditionally because the grant is
always mounted; a device that reads discovery is exactly the client
that cannot be told the URL out of band.

dpop_signing_alg_values_supported.description:
RFC 9449 §5.1 — X5.1 second half. The JWS algorithms AXIAM accepts on a
DPoP proof.

Its **presence** is what tells a client DPoP is supported at all; RFC
9449 defines no separate boolean. The list is the profile's three, and
notably excludes `RS256` — the omission a client library defaulting to
RSA will hit first, and the reason advertising the list matters rather
than merely advertising support.

pushed_authorization_request_endpoint.description:
RFC 9126 §5 — B5. Advertised unconditionally because the endpoint is
always mounted.

require_pushed_authorization_requests.description:
The **server-wide** default, which is `false`: PAR is available to
every client but demanded of none. Per-client enforcement is
`require_par` on the registration and is deliberately not discoverable
— RFC 9126 §5 scopes this metadata to the server, and publishing a
per-client answer here would leak one client's posture to every other
reader of the document.

tls_client_certificate_bound_access_toke.description:
RFC 8705 §3.3 — X5.1. Certificate-bound access tokens are available;
whether a given client *gets* them is that client's
`tls_client_certificate_bound_access_tokens` registration, which is
deliberately not discoverable for the same reason `require_par` is not:
this document is scoped to the server, and a per-client answer here
would leak one client's posture to every reader.

redirect_uri.description:
SPA post-login destination (stored server-side; returned in callback
response body so the SPA can route after receiving cookies).

OidcStartResponse.description:
Response body for `POST /api/v1/auth/federation/oidc/start`.
The nonce is intentionally omitted — it stays server-side (T-04-31).

authorize_url.description: The IdP authorization URL to redirect the user to.

state.description: CSRF state value (must be round-tripped through the IdP).

OpaqueEnrollment.description:
The client-supplied half of an OPAQUE enrolment, as it appears inside
registration / change-password / reset-completion / bootstrap request
bodies.

There is no standalone `register/finish` endpoint, deliberately. A record
can only be created at a moment when the plaintext password legitimately
exists on the client, and every one of those moments is already an endpoint
that takes a password. A free-standing finish would be an endpoint whose
only job is to attach a credential to an account, which is a thing worth
not having.

Kept separate from [`CreateOpaqueCredential`] because the tenant, the user
and the credential identifier are all decided by the server — a client that
could name them could enrol a record against somebody else's account.

opaque_session.description: The `opaque_session` from the register/start response, echoed verbatim.
The `opaque_session` from the login/start response, echoed verbatim.

org_id.description: Organization UUID. Either this or `org_slug` is required.

org_slug.description: Organization slug. Either this or `org_id` is required.

tenant_id.description: Tenant UUID. Either this or `tenant_slug` is required.

tenant_slug.description: Tenant slug. Either this or `tenant_id` is required.

username_or_email.description: Username or email, as typed by the human.

OpaqueLoginStartResponse.description:
Server response to `POST /api/v1/auth/opaque/login/start`.

Every field is safe to return for an identity that does not exist — the
server derives a stable decoy credential identifier and produces a
well-formed `KE2` from it, so this response cannot be used to enumerate
accounts.

Note what is *not* here: the credential identifier itself. It keys the
server's OPRF and never enters the client's computation, so returning it
would be a gratuitous disclosure. This is a real difference from SRP, whose
challenge had to carry the canonical `identity` because that string was
inside the client's key derivation.

iterations.description: Argon2id time cost; absent for scrypt.

memory_kib.description: Argon2id memory cost in KiB; absent for scrypt.

opaque_session.description:
Opaque sealed server state. Must be echoed verbatim to
`/auth/opaque/login/finish`; the client cannot read or forge it.

r.description: scrypt block size; absent for Argon2id.

OpaquePolicy.description:
Secure Remote Password policy.

`suite` and `ksf` are the parameters a *new* registration record is enrolled
with. They deliberately do not apply retroactively: an existing record is
only valid under the suite and KSF it was created with, so tightening these
takes effect as users next set a password rather than invalidating
everybody at once.

opaque_ksf.description:
Key-stretching function new records are enrolled under. Both variants
are memory-hard; see [`opaque_ksf_is_at_least`] for the tighten-only
ordering.

opaque_mode.description: Whether OPAQUE is offered, and whether password login is still accepted.

opaque_suite.description: RFC 9807 ciphersuite new records are enrolled under.

OpaqueRegisterStartRequest.description:
Client request to `POST /api/v1/auth/opaque/register/start`.

Unauthenticated, because it is needed while creating a user who does not
exist yet. That is safe: the server mints the credential identifier itself,
randomly, so an attacker calling this repeatedly obtains OPRF evaluations
under identifiers they did not choose and cannot predict. Had the
identifier been caller-supplied, this would instead be an oracle for
grinding a chosen user's OPRF offline.

org_id.description: Organization UUID. Either this or `org_slug` is required.

org_slug.description: Organization slug. Either this or `org_id` is required.

registration_request.description:
Lowercase-hex serialized RFC 9807 `RegistrationRequest` (a blinded
group element).

tenant_id.description: Tenant UUID. Either this or `tenant_slug` is required.

tenant_slug.description: Tenant slug. Either this or `tenant_id` is required.

iterations.description: Argon2id time cost; absent for scrypt.

ksf.description: KSF the client must stretch with.

memory_kib.description: Argon2id memory cost in KiB; absent for scrypt.

opaque_session.description:
Opaque sealed server state. Must be echoed verbatim to
`/auth/opaque/register/finish`; the client cannot read or forge it.

r.description: scrypt block size; absent for Argon2id.

registration_response.description:
Lowercase-hex serialized RFC 9807 `RegistrationResponse` (the evaluated
element and the server's public key).

Organization.description:
An organization groups multiple tenants under a single administrative entity.

Organizations represent companies, departments, or business units.
CA certificates are registered at the organization level, enabling
a hierarchical trust model across all tenants.

PermissionEffect.description:
Whether a grant permits an action or refuses it (B1, deny-override).

# Precedence

Default deny -> an [`PermissionEffect::Allow`] grant permits ->
a [`PermissionEffect::Deny`] grant refuses, **and beats every allow**,
wherever either sits in the resource hierarchy. Deny wins; there is no
most-specific-wins tie-break.

That choice is deliberate and is argued in full in
`claude_dev/deny-override-design.md` §2.1. The short version: deny-override
buys one checkable property — **adding a deny rule can never widen access,
and can never be undone by adding allows** — and most-specific-wins buys
expressiveness at the cost of making "is X denied?" unanswerable without
enumerating every other rule that might out-specify it.

[`PermissionEffect::Allow`] is the default, so data written before this
existed, and clients that send no `effect`, both mean "allow". No migration.

PermissionGrant.description:
A permission grant with optional scope constraints.
Empty `scope_ids` means the grant covers all scopes (wildcard).

effect.description:
B1: whether this grant permits or refuses. Defaults to
[`PermissionEffect::Allow`], which is what every pre-B1 row and every
`effect`-less request means.

Scope interaction: an empty `scope_ids` is a **wildcard**, so a deny
with no scopes masks the action entirely on this node and its
descendants — every scope, and unscoped checks too. A scoped deny masks
only the scopes it names.

PermissionRequestBody.description:
Body of `POST /uma2/perm` — what the resource server requires.

UMA 2.0 §3.2 allows either a single object or an array; AXIAM accepts the
array form only, because a resource server that needs one pair can send an
array of one, and accepting both shapes means two parsers for one meaning.

PermissionTicketResponse.description: `201 Created` body of the permission endpoint (UMA 2.0 §3.2).

ticket.description: The opaque handle. Returned exactly once — only its hash is stored.

PgpKey.description: An OpenPGP key stored by AXIAM.

PgpKeyPurpose.description: The purpose of an OpenPGP key.

effective_unknown_aaguid.description:
The action actually applied to an AAGUID with no MDS metadata,
with `unknown_aaguid: null` resolved against `mode`. Read-only —
`PUT` ignores it.

PolicyResponse.description:
`GET` response: the stored policy plus the unknown-AAGUID action it
currently *resolves to*.

`unknown_aaguid` is nullable, where `null` means "use this mode's
default" (deny under `direct_required`, allow otherwise). A client that
only saw the stored `null` would have to re-derive that rule itself to
display what the policy actually does — and a security rule implemented
twice is a security rule that will eventually disagree with itself. So
the server resolves it once, here, and reports both: the admin's stored
intent and its effect.

PushedAuthorizationRequest.description:
Form body accepted by `POST /oauth2/par`.

These are the ordinary authorization-request parameters, plus the client
credentials that make the push attributable. `request_uri` is deliberately
absent: RFC 9126 §2.1 forbids pushing one, because a chained push would let
the second request inherit the first's authentication.

client_secret.description:
Optional since SEC-093: a client registered for `tls_client_auth` or
`private_key_jwt` has no secret to present here, and presenting one no
longer authenticates it.

ReactorEventDescriptor.description: One hookable event, as the registry describes it.

mutable_fields.description:
Exact field names, or a namespace prefix ending in `.` — `ext.` admits
`ext.department` and nothing outside the namespace.

ReactorMode.description: How a reactor participates in an event.

last_seen_at.description:
When this reactor last consumed from its queue. `null` means it has
never connected — which the admin UI shows differently from "connected
once, silent since".

recent_timeout_count.description:
R2.3: dispatch failures against this registration in the last 24h
whose cause was a timeout (as opposed to a rejected reply, a transport
failure, or overload), capped at 100 — a health signal read from the
audit trail R2.2 started writing, not a replacement for the audit log
itself (`GET /api/v1/audit-log` is that).

recent_veto_count.description:
R2.3: operations this reactor's own reply *denied* in the last 24h,
capped at 100. Distinct from `recent_timeout_count`: a veto is the
reactor working as designed; a timeout is the reactor not answering.

RefreshSuccessResponse.description:
Refresh success response body.

The new access token is delivered via `Set-Cookie` headers.

RequestResetBody.description:
Body for the request-reset endpoint.

`tenant_id` is optional (Open Question 1 / Assumption A4): the public
forgot-password page has no prior tenant context, so it may instead
supply `org_slug`/`tenant_slug` (mirroring `handlers/auth.rs`'s
`(Option<Uuid>, Option<&str>)` login pattern). Slug-resolution failure
is enumeration-safe (D-05) — it funnels into the SAME uniform
`{"sent": true}` response as an unknown account, never a distinct
error status.

RequestedPermission.description:
One `(resource, scopes)` pair a resource server requires, as posted to
`/uma2/perm`.

resource_id.description:
The AXIAM resource id. UMA's `_id` **is** the AXIAM resource id — there
is no parallel resource store to translate through.

resource_scopes.description:
Scope names, each of which must be declared by the resource. Matched
exactly: no prefix or wildcard semantics in either direction.

ResetContextResponse.description:
What a valid reset-token holder needs in order to build an OPAQUE record.

The SRP version of this also returned the account's `identity`, because
SRP derived its private key over `username ":" password` and the reset page
had no other way to learn the username. OPAQUE binds to a server-chosen
credential identifier that the client never handles, so the username is not
needed and is no longer disclosed. The endpoint went from "tell an
unauthenticated caller who this account is" to "tell them whether this
tenant uses OPAQUE", which is strictly less.

oneOf.description:
The tenant's effective OPAQUE policy, so the client knows whether to
run an enrolment at all. Absent when the tenant does not use OPAQUE.

parent_id.description: Parent resource ID for hierarchical organization. `None` for root resources.

uma_registered_by.description:
The `client_id` that registered this resource through the UMA
Protection API (X2), or `None` for a resource created any other way.

Read-only from every ordinary path: [`UpdateResource`] cannot set it and
[`CreateResource`] cannot either, so the only writer is the
resource-registration handler. That is deliberate — the field backs a
provenance badge in the admin UI, and a provenance marker anyone can
write is decoration that reads like evidence.

ResourceSet.description:
A resource set as UMA describes it, mapped onto an AXIAM resource.

# The mapping, in one place

| UMA | AXIAM |
|---|---|
| `_id` | the resource id — **not** a parallel identifier |
| `name` | `resource.name` |
| `type` | `resource.resource_type` |
| `resource_scopes` | the `Scope` rows on that resource |

There is no second resource store. A resource registered here is an
ordinary AXIAM resource that the admin UI lists, that role assignments
cascade through, and that the authorization engine already understands —
which is the entire reason UMA `_id` is the AXIAM id rather than a
translation key.

_id.description: Present on responses, absent on registration — the server assigns it.

RetryPolicy.description: Retry policy for failed webhook deliveries.

initial_delay_secs.description: Initial delay between retries in seconds.

RevokeRequest.description:
RFC 7009 token revocation request.

`client_secret` is optional and the two RFC 7521 assertion parameters are
present because RFC 7009 §2.1 says this endpoint authenticates the client
"the same way as the token endpoint" — and since SEC-093 it genuinely does.
A client registered for `private_key_jwt` posts `client_assertion` here and
no secret; one registered for `tls_client_auth` posts neither and is
authenticated by the certificate on the connection.

is_global.description: Global roles grant permissions across all resources.

RoleAssignment.description: A role together with its assignment context (the resource it is scoped to).

resource_id.description: `None` means the role was assigned globally (no resource scope).

RptPermission.description:
One entry of an RPT's `permissions` claim.

Field names are Keycloak's (`rsid`/`rsname` aliases aside) so that a
resource server migrating from Keycloak can read an AXIAM RPT without a
translation layer — the compatibility the §X2 introspection test pins.

exp.description:
Absolute expiry, seconds since the epoch. Carried per-permission
because UMA allows an RPT to accumulate permissions with different
lifetimes; AXIAM issues them uniformly in v1 but the shape must not
foreclose that.

ScimTokenResponse.description:
Metadata only. The handle is never in a list response — it exists in
plaintext exactly once, in [`CreateScimTokenResponse`].

ScimTokenStatus.description:
Why a token is or is not currently usable — for display only. The
authentication path never surfaces this distinction on the wire.

resource_id.description: The resource this scope belongs to.

SecuritySettings.description: Fully resolved security settings (all fields present).

description.description: Optional human-readable description of the account's purpose.

ServiceAccountCreatedResponse.description: Response for service account creation — includes the one-time plaintext secret.

SetOrgEmailConfig.description: Input for setting organization-level email config.

SetOrgSettings.description: Input for setting organization-level security settings.

SettingsScope.description: Whether a settings row belongs to an organization or a tenant.

SignAuditBatchRequest.description: Request body for signing an audit batch.

SignedAuditBatch.description: A signed batch of audit log entries.

signature_armored.description: ASCII-armored PGP signed message containing the audit batch payload.

SmtpConfig.description:
SMTP-specific configuration.

`password` is write-only (D-01): `#[serde(skip_serializing)]` means it is
never emitted in a GET/serialized response. On the write path (D-02),
`#[serde(default)]` lets a caller omit the field entirely (deserializing
to `""`); an empty string is the sentinel for "no new secret supplied —
preserve whatever is already stored" (see `SurrealEmailConfigRepository::
set_org_config`). A non-empty value is a real secret to encrypt+replace.

SsoLoginSuccessResponse.description:
Returned by both OIDC callback and SAML ACS on success (alongside
Set-Cookie headers). The `redirect_uri` field allows the SPA to route
the user to the originally requested destination.

redirect_uri.description: SPA destination URL stored during start/login.

Tenant.description:
A tenant is an isolated context within an organization.

Each tenant has its own set of users, roles, permissions, resources,
certificates, and configuration. Tenants can represent environments
(dev/staging/prod) or separate business contexts.

organization_id.description: The organization this tenant belongs to.

slug.description: URL-safe unique identifier within the organization (e.g., `production`).

status.description: Lifecycle status. New tenants default to [`TenantStatus::Active`].

TenantSettingsOverride.description: Partial tenant overrides. `None` = inherit from org baseline.

TenantStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a tenant.

A `Suspended` tenant remains stored and its data isolated, but is treated as
administratively disabled. New tenants are `Active` by default.

actor_token.description:
Presence of an actor token selects **delegation**; absence selects
**impersonation**, which is off unless the client is granted it.

audience.description:
Target audience for the issued token. **The allow-list is the
client's `redirect_uris`** (SEC-089): a target is accepted if it
appears in the client's registered redirect URIs, or is one of
AXIAM's own built-in audiences. There is no separate audience field
in v1 — adding a redirect URI to a client also authorises it as a
token audience for that client. This allow-list is checked at two
call sites in this file (same-domain exchange, and the X4 external
exchange) — both are tagged `SEC-089` and must be touched together
(and together with this comment) if a future dedicated
`allowed_token_targets` field replaces this reuse. Full write-up in
`docs/api/token-exchange.md#audience`.

requested_token_type.description:
RFC 8693 §2.1. Optional, and the AS picks the default — but a client
that *names* a type it does not get must be told, not handed an
access token and left to discover the difference. v1 issues access
tokens only, so any other explicit value is refused.

resource.description:
RFC 8707. Treated as a synonym of `audience`; if both are given they
must agree, because silently preferring one would make the request
mean something the caller did not write.

scope.description: Space-separated. Absent means "the subject's own scopes".

issued_token_type.description:
Mandatory per §2.2.1, and not decoration: a client that asked for one
token type and got another must be able to tell.

TokenExchangeTrustRequest.description:
X4 trust for exchanging this provider's tokens (RFC 8693, external issuer).

Mirrors [`TokenExchangeTrust`] on the wire rather than reusing it directly
so the API surface can carry its own defaults: an admin PUTting a partial
block gets the documented default for anything they omitted, instead of a
deserialization error listing fields they have never heard of.

accepted_audiences.description:
Audiences an incoming subject token may name. Required (non-empty)
when `enabled`; there is deliberately no accept-all value.

enabled.description:
Off unless explicitly enabled. Configuring a provider for *login* is
not agreement to accept its tokens as API credentials.

max_lifetime_secs.description: Per-provider ceiling on the issued AXIAM token's lifetime.

max_token_age_secs.description: Bound on `now - iat`, independent of the token's own `exp`.

scope_map.description:
External asserted value -> AXIAM scopes. Deny-by-default: an external
value with no entry contributes nothing.

TokenExchangeTrustResponse.description:
X4 trust as returned. Same shape as the request; nothing here is secret —
an operator reading a provider needs to see exactly what it trusts.

claim_token.description:
The requesting party's identity, as an AXIAM access token.

UMA 2.0 §3.3.1 makes this optional because a client may instead present
its own RPT for incremental authorization, which v1 does not implement.
With claims-gathering also deferred, this is the only channel through
which a requesting party can be named — so the grant requires it and
says so, rather than resolving to some default subject.

claim_token_format.description:
Declared format of `claim_token`. Only the AXIAM access-token URN is
accepted in v1; anything else is refused rather than guessed at.

client_assertion.description:
The signed JWT a `private_key_jwt` client authenticates with.

Carried here rather than in a second form type for the same reason the
RFC 8693 parameters are: actix deserializes one body once, and the
token endpoint cannot know which client-authentication method applies
until it has read `client_id` out of that body and loaded the
registration.

device_code.description:
B2 — the secret a device polls with, for
`grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`
(RFC 8628 §3.4). Present only on that grant; the REST layer routes it
to [`crate::device_service::DeviceAuthorizationService`] rather than
to [`TokenService::exchange`], which never sees it.

ticket.description:
The permission ticket minted by `/uma2/perm`, for
`grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:uma-ticket`.

permission_ticket_lifetime.description:
Advertised so a resource server can size its retry window against the
ticket TTL instead of discovering it by having a ticket expire.

UnknownAaguidAction.description:
What to do with an AAGUID that has no MDS entry (i.e. FIDO Alliance has
no metadata for it — not necessarily malicious, MDS coverage is
incomplete for some legitimate authenticators).

idp_signing_cert_pem.description:
PEM-encoded X.509 certificate for verifying SAML assertions
(CQ-B40/REQ-14 AC-5).  `Some(None)` clears the stored cert.

oneOf.description:
X4 external token-exchange trust. Replaced **wholesale** when present:
a partial merge of a trust configuration is how an operator ends up
keeping an `accepted_audiences` entry they believed they had removed.

backchannel_logout_uri.description:
Pass an empty string to clear a previously registered URI — the one
edit an operator makes when an RP is decommissioned.

jwks.description:
X5.1 — see the create DTO. `Some("")` clears, so a client can be
migrated from an inline key set to a published one.

jwks_uri.description: X5.1 — see the create DTO. `Some("")` clears.

tls_client_auth_subject_dn.description: Pass an empty string to clear, as with `backchannel_logout_uri`.

UpdateOrganization.description: Fields that can be updated on an existing organization.

metadata.description: Free-form metadata (the admin UI stores `description` here).

UpdateTenant.description: Fields that can be updated on an existing tenant.

oneOf.description: Change the tenant's lifecycle status (e.g. suspend/reactivate).

secret.description:
New HMAC-SHA256 shared secret (D-02 secret rotation). Encrypted
server-side with AES-256-GCM before storage; omit to leave the
existing secret untouched.

deletion_pending.description: GDPR Art. 17 — set when user requests account deletion (D-08).

mfa_secret.description: AES-256-GCM encrypted TOTP secret (if MFA is enrolled).

scheduled_purge_at.description: Scheduled purge date when `deletion_pending` is true (D-08).

totp_last_used_step.description:
The TOTP time-step counter value last successfully verified.

Used to prevent replay attacks: a code whose step ≤ this value is
rejected even if the HMAC is correct (SEC-008).

UserResponse.description: Public-safe user representation (no password_hash, no mfa_secret).

email_verified.description:
True when the user's email address has been verified
(`email_verified_at` is set). Exposed for the admin UI / profile.

failed_login_attempts.description: Number of consecutive failed login attempts.

is_locked.description: Whether the account is currently locked (locked_until is in the future).

locked_until.description: Timestamp until which the account is locked, if any.

VerifyResponse.description:
The consent screen's data. Deliberately minimal: a client id and the
scopes being asked for. Nothing here identifies the device or its network.

found.description: `false` for unknown, expired, or already-decided codes alike.

WebauthnAttestationPolicy.description:
Per-tenant WebAuthn attestation policy (D5). One row per tenant; an
absent row means [`WebauthnAttestationPolicy::default`], which is
today's behavior unchanged.

allowed_aaguids.description:
`None` = every AAGUID is allowed except `blocked_aaguids`.

`Some(vec![])` is a deliberate "nothing may register" policy and is
accepted as such: `evaluate` denies every AAGUID against an empty
allow-list. Nothing rejects it, precisely because the failure
direction is safe — a client that sends `[]` when it meant `null`
gets a locked-down tenant, which is visible immediately, rather than
an open one, which is not.

block_revoked_status.description:
Deny registration if the MDS entry has ever reported `REVOKED` or any
`*_COMPROMISE` status (sticky — D8 step 7).

require_fido_certified.description:
Require *some* `FIDO_CERTIFIED*` status, any level. Independent of
(and checked before) `min_certification`.

oneOf.description:
What to do with an AAGUID MDS has no metadata for.

`None` means "use the default for this `mode`", which is **deny under
`direct_required` and allow otherwise** — see
[`WebauthnAttestationPolicy::effective_unknown_aaguid`]. It is
deliberately an `Option` rather than a plain value with a fixed
default: a single struct-level default cannot be correct for both
modes, and the one that is wrong is wrong in the dangerous direction.
A tenant that opts into the strictest posture and does not mention
this field would otherwise admit every authenticator FIDO has no
metadata for — silently, with no error and nothing in the audit trail
to suggest the policy was not doing what its name says.

An explicit `Some(_)` always wins, in both directions: an admin who
deliberately wants `direct_required` *and* lenient handling of
unlisted authenticators can still say so.

WebhookResponse.description: Webhook response — omits the shared secret.
